newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO helicopter chases Bosnian police after arson.
newsitem.headline: NATO helicopter chases Bosnian police after arson.

text.p: A NATO peace force helicopter chased a Bosnian police car after spotting it racing away from burning Serb-owned houses, international officials said on Wednesday.
U.N. police monitors launched an inquiry into the behaviour of local police in the Moslem-dominated area of the Bosnian Federation after the incident on Tuesday.
A cluster of homes in a northwestern village abandoned by Serbs during Bosnia's 1992-95 war was going up in flames when a patrolling NATO helicopter happened by, an NATO spokesman said.

"The helicopter saw several buildings on fire several kilometres (miles) north of Kljuc and then a vehicle with five passengers heading away from the scene at a high rate of speed," Major Brett Boudreau said at a news briefing.
"The helicopter followed the vehicle for several km to (another village) in the Federation where the passengers jumped out of the car and entered a house," he said.
"Canadian (NATO) soldiers were despatched to the house and found it was a police station. And the individuals identified themselves as Bosnian police officers."

A spokesman for the U.N.-affiliated International Police Task Force (IPTF) which monitors law-enforcement and human rights in Bosnia said the targeted houses had belonged to Serbs who fled during the war.
Under the 1995 Dayton peace treaty signed by Moslem, Serb and Croat factions, war refugees were to be allowed to cross entity boundary lines and reclaim their homes.
But many deserted homes in both the Moslem-Croat Federation and Serb Republic in Bosnia have been blown up by nationalist militants, sometimes local policemen, to discourage refugees from returning.
